subject: Canary containment playbook & temporary pin authorization
messages:

Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: latency spike during canary — request containment plan

Hey Jordan / Laura,

We just observed a consistent 3x 95th percentile latency increase on the canary cohort for the /chat endpoint between 08:30–09:00 PST. Errors were low, but the latency tail is causing timeouts upstream (BrightFin payment flow). We've rolled the canary down manually for the moment, but our front line is asking for a short-lived formal containment and rollback policy we can rely on during launches.

Questions:
- Can Redwood support an automatic fallback to the prior pinned model variant for canaries that breach a latency gate?
- Can we request a temporary pin (version lock) while BrightFin completes their verification window?

We need a documented playbook and an authorization artifact we can show our legal/procurement team (they asked for a signed exception for anything that affects SLA windows).

Attached: sample traces and the canary metrics snapshot.

Thanks,
Tara Shah
Platform Lead, BrightFin
ops+prod@brightfin.com

Attachments: brightfin_canary_traces_20261212.zip (log bundle)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Tara Shah <ops+prod@brightfin.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: latency spike during canary — request containment plan

Tara — thanks for the quick heads-up and the trace bundle. Sorry you hit that.

Short answer: yes. We have a containment playbook that covers automatic fallback, short-term pinning, and traffic quarantine. I'm attaching the playbook PDF and a one-page temporary-pin authorization template we can sign. High-level proposal (so you have it in writing right away):

1) Immediate containment (we can enact automatically):
   - If 95th percentile latency > 1.8x baseline for two consecutive 5-minute buckets OR error-rate jump > 0.5%, gateway routes automatically shift 100% to the last stable model variant (version pin), with an option to route only new sessions depending on your session affinity settings.
   - Concurrently, spawn a short retention trace and stop client-side retries for canary cohort to avoid storming.

2) Short-term pin:
   - Request a temporary pin of the stable model for up to 72 hours while we triage with you. Pin can be extended by mutual written consent.

3) Telemetry gates (required to unpin):
   - Stability: 95p latency and p99 both within 10% of baseline for a rolling 3-hour window.
   - Quality: sample prompt evals pass the agreed prompt-set regression checks (link in playbook).

4) SLA carveout & customer communication:
   - If BrightFin asks, we can issue a signed temporary exception for the SLA window covering the pin. This is not an admission of breach; it allows BrightFin to avoid hitting automated penalty triggers while we investigate. Legal needs to sign the attached template.

Next steps I propose:
- I will open a formal pin request and start the automatic fallback policy for the canary (requires your ACK).
- If you want the signed exception, reply with the redlines and I'll loop Legal.

Attaching: canary_containment_playbook_v2.pdf, temporary-pin-authorization-template.docx

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Jordan / Tara — fine with the containment thresholds Jordan proposed. A couple of operational asks before I sign anything:

- Add an automatic alert into the BrightFin incident channel that the fallback executed, with the exact rule trigger and the pre/post latency snapshot. We should avoid silent pins.
- Limit the first pin to 24 hours by default; Marcus, I'm asking you to confirm we can escalate to 72 hours only with cross-functional signoff (SRE + CS + Legal).
- Include an explicit rollback-for-analysis window so we can run offline regressions against the canary dataset without impacting traffic.

Tara: if you confirm ACK to the automatic fallback (you can reply-all with "ACK - automatic fallback"), I'll sign the temporary-pin template and instruct Legal to fast-track signoff.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
